title: What is known about 1RB0RA_1LC0LE_1RA1LD_0LB1LF_1LD0RC_1LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_1LC0LE_1RA1LD_0LB1LF_1LD0RC_1LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The sweep, the phase and the two clean phase ends are proved in Lean for all values (kernel); blank tape reaches the clean regime at step 58,429 (native_decide) and four clean phases follow by the kernel. The exact cycle accelerator runs 101000 steps without a halt. The phase end for y ≡ 1 (mod 3) and the resets of deeper levels are not yet closed rules.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: One sweep, for all values
claims.text: From 0^∞ C> 0 1 0 (110)^p 1111 (110)^x 11100 (100)^(y+3) R the machine reaches the same form with (x+4, y) in 8p + 24x + 75 steps, for every p, x, y and every tape R.

claims.title: A phase of k sweeps
claims.text: (x, 3k + y) to (x + 4k, y), by induction on k, with the exact step count pst.

claims.title: The clean phase ends
claims.text: When y comes down to 0 or 2 the front level is reset to (0, x) or (0, x + 2), the counter p gains 2 and the next level (z, w) becomes (z + 2, w − 2). Together: on an empty front level y ↦ 4y/3 (y ≡ 0) and y ↦ 4(y − 2)/3 + 2 (y ≡ 2).

claims.title: Blank tape enters the clean regime
claims.text: After 58,429 steps the tape is cfg 2 (lv 0 72 (lv 12 26 (lv 10 3 (lv 2 1 (lv 2 0 (lv 2 0 11)))))); four clean phases (kernel) take y through 72, 96, 128, 170, 226 and reach step 399,523, exactly where the simulator sees that tape.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>1000</sup> steps
claims.text: The shared cycle accelerator (bbtools.cycles on 3-cell blocks; every jump applies a cycle rule proved symbolically) runs 101000 steps in about seven minutes, with 5,609 rules and 3,726 jumps, and no halt.

claims.title: A Collatz-like counter
claims.text: The residue of y mod 3 at the end of each phase looks irregular; y ≡ 1 starts a secondary bouncer that rebuilds the left part, and the run returns to the clean form with p = 0. Levels further right are reset in turn, each a bit longer than before.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly when D reads a 1 with a 1 to its left (C at 1 1 C>1 or E at 1 1 E>0); the proved rules never do that, but the y ≡ 1 regime and the deep resets are not closed rules yet.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RE_1LC1RD_1LA0LC_0RA1RF_1RD0LB_1RA--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine builds a row of counters on its tape. The front counter grows by a factor of about 4/3 each round, and whether the count is divisible by 3 decides what happens next, just like in the Collatz problem. It has been followed for 10<sup>1000</sup> steps without stopping.

facts.text: The clean phase map, proved for all values.
Blank tape reaches the clean regime.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.604). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 46,692 cells (39,843 left of the start, 35 right), with a density of 1s of 0.386.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: What the tape is made of
html: Read the tape in words of three cells: 110 (drawn in the accent colour) and 100 (grey). Whenever the head is back at the left end, in state C, the tape is: a short start 0 1 0, a counter of 110s, a marker 1111, and then a row of levels. A level is a run of 110s, a separator 11100 (orange) and a run of 100s. The first level is the front; write it (x, y).

Exactly: (x, y + 3) → (x + 4, y) in 8p + 24x + 75 steps. A phase is ⌊y/3⌋ sweeps in a row.

sections.heading: A counter that multiplies by 4/3
html: When the 100s of the front run out, the remainder r = y mod 3 decides what happens.

rnew frontnext levelcounter
0(0, x)(z + 2, w − 2)p + 2
2(0, x + 2)(z + 2, w − 2)p + 2
1a different regime: secondary bouncers rebuild the counter into new levels, and the run comes back with p = 0
Since a phase of ⌊y/3⌋ sweeps adds 4 to x each time, a front that starts empty ends with x = 4⌊y/3⌋, so the new front is
y ↦ 4y/3 if y ≡ 0,   y ↦ 4(y − 2)/3 + 2 if y ≡ 2 (mod 3).

From step 58,429 the front goes 72 → 96 → 128 → 170 → 226, and 226 ≡ 1 ends the clean run. Later: 734 → 978 → 1304 → 1738 ≡ 1. Each reset also ticks the next level, two words at a time; when that level's 100s run out it is reset in turn and ticks the one after it: a mixed-radix counter whose digits get longer every time they are reset. Because y grows geometrically and a phase costs about y² steps, the tape grows like the square root of time.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is F reading 1. F is entered only from D reading 1, so the machine halts exactly when D reads a 1 that has a 1 on its left: C at 1 1 C>1 or E at 1 1 E>0. The sweeps and the clean phase ends never do that (they are proved for all values). What is not yet written as a rule is the y ≡ 1 regime and the reset of the levels far to the right; those are where a halt would have to come from.

sections.heading: What is proved
html:
• Kernel: the sweep, the phase (any number of sweeps), the two clean phase ends and the 4/3 map (lean/Rules.lean, lean/Macro.lean).
  • native_decide: blank tape reaches the clean regime after 58,429 steps; four clean phases then reach step 399,523 (lean/Start.lean).
  • Trusted computation: no halt in 101000 steps (exact cycle accelerator).
  • Open: whether it ever halts.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0RE_1LC1RD_1LA0LC_0RA1RF_1RD0LB_1RA---: rename A→C, B→A, C→B, D→D, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror

summary: A row of counter levels W^x 11100 V^y; each sweep turns three 100s into four 110s, so a phase maps the front level y to about 4y/3 (y mod 3 decides the branch) and ticks the next level; no halt in 10^1000 steps.
